title: Learn Faster, Perform Better: A Musician's Guide to the Neuroscience of Practicing
description: Practicing is an essential part of every musician's life, but we are rarely taught how to practice in the most effective and efficient way. Many of us find ourselves frustrated when we sound good in the practice room only to embarrass ourselves on stage or in front of our teachers. We feel overwhelmed by the amount of music we have to learn, unsure how to balance everything. Playing from memory can feel terrifying and an insurmountable challenge, and overcoming bad habits can seem impossible at times. Molly Gebrian applies the science of learning and memory to practicing and performing, giving musicians the tools to learn music more effectively and experience greater confidence on stage. Researchers working in the fields of cognitive psychology and neuroscience have discovered many important principles about how the brain learns new information, retains this information both short- and long-term, and how to make this learning reliable in high-pressure situations like performances. Musicians often choose practice strategies that don't align well with the optimal ways in which the brain learns, leading to frustration while practicing and inconsistency in performance. The author offers a practical guide, using accessible language for non-scientists and non-academics, to help musicians get more out of their practicing by applying this research. Gebrian starts with general principles of learning and how the brain works, and then progresses through increasingly specific topics. title: How to Learn Anything Faster: 8 Simple Methods for Effective Learning
description: Stop studying harder—start learning smarter. Most people learn the way they were taught in school: read the material, highlight the important parts, and read it again before a test. While it feels productive, rereading and highlighting only create a false sense of familiarity—which is why so many people study for hours and still forget most of what they covered within a few days. The problem is not your effort. It is your method. How to Learn Anything Faster: 8 Simple Methods for Effective Learning offers a practical, step-by-step toolkit designed to match the way your memory actually works. Because the way you practice matters more than how long you practice, a shorter session built on the right method can help you remember far more than a long session built on the wrong one. Inside this book, you will discover eight straightforward methods you can use on their own or combine together: • Active Recall: Test yourself on information instead of simply rereading your notes to strengthen memory pathways. • Spaced Repetition: Review material at increasing intervals over days and weeks rather than cramming in one sitting. • Teach It Simply: Explain concepts in plain, everyday words to immediately spot and fill gaps in your understanding. • Chunking: Break large, overwhelming topics into small, manageable clusters. • The Memory Palace: Link new facts and sequences to familiar spatial locations you already know well. • Focused Time Blocks: Study in short, concentrated periods followed by planned breaks to prevent mental fatigue. • A Distraction-Free Setup: Arrange your physical space and digital devices so that focused study becomes the easiest option. • Mixed Practice: Alternate between related problem types and skills to build deeper, more flexible understanding. It is not simply about reading about learning, but about starting to apply what you learn from the very beginning. This book can help you: • Organize your study sessions more effectively. • Remember information for longer. • Avoid passive rereading and study more actively. • Improve your concentration and reduce distractions. • Identify and correct your mistakes. • Overcome procrastination and develop consistency. • Use practice to turn knowledge into skills. • Create a personal learning system you can maintain.
